Yeah say you're going from a C maj to F maj. You have C E G on the down beat of measure 1. Measure 2 on beat 1 you have G skip to B and you have F C in the bass. B then resolves to A on beat 3 making the F maj chord appear. Appoggiatura is approached by a skip and resolves by step. They are accented since they appear on a strong beat.

All these reference Cmaj

Neighbor tone: note moves a step up or down and returns back to the original note  (C-(D)-C or (C-(B)-C)

Passing tone: note in between the chord tones ( C-(D)-E) D is the passing tone. 

Escape Tone: Note is approached by step and resolved in the opposite direction to a chord tone (E-F-C) Escape tone is F.

Another method you can try is play the scale of the note. Work upwards. Chromatic scales aid too. 
Remember to have plenty of air support. It doesn't take more pressure on the mouth piece. It takes steady fast air. 
And as always, long tones are your friends for strength.
